# Employment Data Analysis - Complete Report

## 📋 Analysis Overview

This comprehensive analysis of **employment-data.csv** has been completed successfully. The dataset contains **20,108 records** of New Zealand employment statistics from the Business Data Collection (BDC), spanning **Q2 2011 to Q2 2025** (14 years).

## 🔍 Key Findings Summary

### Dataset Characteristics
- **Total Records:** 20,108
- **Time Span:** 14 years (2011-2025)
- **Frequency:** Quarterly (Feb, May, Aug, Nov)
- **Data Completeness:** 91.46%
- **Suppressed Data:** 8.54%

### Dimensions Analyzed
- ✅ **5 Category Groups:** Industry, Age, Gender, Region, Territorial Authority
- ✅ **10 Industries:** From Agriculture to Arts & Recreation
- ✅ **11 Age Groups:** 15-19 through 65+
- ✅ **16 Regions:** All major NZ regions
- ✅ **68 Territorial Authorities:** District-level granularity
- ✅ **3 Employment Variables:** Filled jobs, Total earnings, Workplace-based jobs

### Top Insights

#### 🏆 Highest Growth Sectors
1. **Electricity, Gas, Water & Waste:** +63.45%
2. **Mining:** +16.66%
3. **Agriculture, Forestry & Fishing:** +15.05%

#### 👥 Demographic Highlights
- **65+ age group:** +108.54% (more than doubled!)
- **30-34 age group:** +60.85% (career-building surge)
- **15-24 age groups:** Slowest growth (youth employment challenge)

#### 🌍 Regional Champions
- **Tasman:** +95.86% (nearly doubled)
- **Northland:** +41.47%
- **Auckland:** +37.84% (largest absolute growth)
- **Nelson:** -20.05% (only declining region)

#### ⚖️ Gender Parity
- **Female:** +31.13% growth
- **Male:** +30.58% growth
- **Gap:** Females now slightly ahead (parity achieved!)

#### 📅 COVID-19 Impact
- **2020 Growth:** +1.09% (slowest but still positive)
- **Recovery:** Strong rebound in 2021-2023
- **Resilience:** Minimal long-term disruption
